A series of three panels showing the Exfoliation process. Panel 1: A solid granite rock under a blazing yellow sun, with red arrows pointing outwards to show expansion. Panel 2: The same rock under a moon and stars with blue arrows pointing inwards showing contraction, and a few small cracks appearing parallel to the surface. Panel 3: Curved outer sheets of the rock peeling away like onion skins, leaving a rounded dome core. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A cross-section of a gentle grassy hillside illustrating Soil Creep. A large tree has a trunk that curves outward at the base before growing straight up. A wooden fence is leaning downhill. A telegraph pole is also leaning downhill. Small blue arrows in the soil point slowly down the slope to indicate the creeping movement of the earth. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A four-panel step-by-step diagram showing Ox-bow lake formation. Panel 1: A river flowing in a wide curve (meander), with arrows showing fast water eroding the outer bank. Panel 2: The neck of land between the two loops becomes very narrow. Panel 3: The river cuts straight across the neck during a flood. Panel 4: The old loop is cut off by deposition at its ends, forming a crescent-shaped ox-bow lake, while the main river flows straight. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A split diagram of wind landforms. On the left, an erosional Rock Pedestal: a large rounded rock resting on a very thin, severely eroded column, surrounded by flying sand particles carried by horizontal wind arrows near the ground. On the right, a depositional Barchan Dune: a smooth crescent-shaped hill of golden sand, with wind arrows hitting the gently sloping back and the two pointed "horns" pointing forward in the direction of the wind. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
